subject: Q3 account stability sweep — exec attention items & risk ledger
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Q3 account stability sweep — exec attention items & risk ledger

Team —

Attached: Q3_acme_health_snapshot.xlsx (sheet: summary + token trends).

Quick ask: we need a concise ledger of items that should land on the exec QBR readout for Acme. I want the list to be prioritized (P1: immediate exec attention, P2: watch/mitigation, P3: operational/owner-only).

Please add one line per risk (owner, current impact, next step, ETA). Ill consolidate into the exec slide and forward to Jordan/Laura by Friday EOD. Specific areas Im most worried about:
- Persistent latency variance on large-batch inference (seen in prod from 8/10 onward)
- Billing overrun from a short-lived spike in embedding jobs (finance asking for context)
- Procurement timeline uncertainty — Acme has indicated procurement signoff may slip into October unless DocuSign MA-P is updated

Owners: Jordan (SLA/redlines), Stephanie (ops mitigations & runbook updates), Laura (exec ask wording and escalation language).

Examples to include in your rows (copy/paste):
- P1 | Latency variance | Owner: Stephanie | Impact: customer-facing latency spikes for batch jobs, 95th p increased to 1.9s | Next step: throttle batch size, enable per-customer KV-cache; ETA: 48h
- P2 | Contract cadence risk | Owner: Jordan | Impact: renewal compressed to 3-week window | Next step: confirm final MA-P and procurement PO path; ETA: EOW

Put updates in this thread. Ill pull into a one-page exec note.

Thanks —
Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Head of Account Strategy | Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2027 10:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q3 account stability sweep — exec attention items & risk ledger

Kimberly —

I started a running ledger (see below). Ill attach a short MA-P redline (mutual_action_plan_v2.docx) that reflects the procurement asks Acmes legal sent yesterday. Two quick notes:

1) SLA clause: Acme is requesting a 12-month availability SLA with credits that are heavier than our standard. Were planning a single-point exception ask for the execs (if needed) vs a permanent change.
2) Finance wants a brief explanation for the embedding spike (customer ran a large similarity job on 8/18). Suggest we include the token counts and mitigation plan.

Ledger (work-in-progress):
- P1 | Latency variance | Owner: Stephanie | Impact: 95th percentile shifts; customer-reported flakiness for large-batch inferences | Next: schedule immediate batch throttling + kernel tuning; ETA: 48h
- P1 | SLA exception request | Owner: Jordan | Impact: potential credit exposure if we dont get pre-approval | Next: Draft exec ask + fallback model variant; ETA: 72h
- P2 | Procurement slip risk | Owner: Jordan | Impact: renewal timeline compressed to Oct | Next: push DocuSign + procurement contact, confirm PO requirements; ETA: 5 days
- P3 | Operational runbook gaps | Owner: Stephanie | Impact: longer MTTR for region failover | Next: confirm on-call runbook updates; ETA: 1 week

Ill also ping product infra to see if a quantized variant can be surfaced as a fallback to reduce cost exposure.

-Jordan
Jordan Blake
VP, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
From: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@acmecorp.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acmecorp.com>, Jonah Reed <jonah.ciso@acmecorp.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2027 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q3 account stability sweep — exec attention items & risk ledger

Kimberly —

Thanks for the heads up and the snapshot. A few items from Acmes side: 

1) Procurement: we need the updated MA-P (we received version v1 but legal flagged section 6.2 and requested the limit on credits be capped). Can you send the redline + a proposed short-term credit cap for the execs to consider?
2) Security: Jonah asked for the SOC2 evidence package and a short note on data retention by environment (prod vs staging). Our auditors want that by 9/10 to keep our renewal timeline intact.
3) Latency: engineering noticed one window on 8/18 where a bulk similarity job caused ripple effects; wed like to understand your throttling fallback and whether KV-prefix caching can be toggled per-customer.

Attaching: acme_po_request.pdf (procurement placeholder).

If you can get the MA-P redline and a 1-paragraph exec ask for credit exception by Monday, we can present it to our procurement committee on 9/8.

Regards,
Sara Jenkins
Senior Program Manager, Platform Integrations
Acme Corp
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 4 Sep 2027 11:32:00 -0700
Subject: Consolidated exec note for Acme QBR (highlights + asks)

Team / Execs —

Attached: consolidated one-pager (Ill upload slide to drive). Below is the executive summary I plan to include in the QBR readout. Please reply with any edits by EOD Sunday. If I dont hear back Ill send to Acme Monday morning.

Executive highlights (TL;DR)
- Stability: Recent 95th percentile regression tied to a large customer similarity job on 8/18; ops has a 48h mitigation (batch throttling + KV-prefix caching toggles) that reduces customer impact by ~70%. Owner: Stephanie.
- Contract: Acme has requested a temporary credit cap change in the MA-P. Recommendation: approve a one-time, limited credit cap tied to performance remediation milestones rather than a permanent SLA change. Owner: Jordan.
- Procurement timeline: Acmes procurement indicates they will review the updated MA-P on 9/8; we should have a signed PO by 9/15 if redline is accepted. Owner: Jordan.

Exec asks (for Jordan/Laura):
1) Approve the approach to a one-time credit-cap exception (draft language attached). If approved, this will be presented to Acme procurement next week.
2) Authorize an interim fallback model (quantized variant) to be used automatically if latency thresholds breach again during the renewal window. This reduces cost exposure and buys time for infra fixes.
3) Sign off on the short security evidence packet to send Jonah by 9/10 (SOC2 excerpt + retention table).

Risk ledger snapshot (top 3):
- P1: Latency variance | Impact: customer experience + potential feature gating | Mitigation: throttle + KV toggles | ETA: 48h
- P1: SLA credit ask | Impact: financial exposure if denied | Mitigation: one-time cap + milestones | ETA: 72h to draft exec ask
- P2: Procurement slip | Impact: renewal timing | Mitigation: DocuSign push + procurement outreach | ETA: 1 week

If we get exec approval on the three asks, Ill finalize the MA-P redline and the one-paragraph credit ask for Acme on Monday. Links: https://hubspot.company/contacts/ACME-12345 | https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1ABCqbrPrepDocs

Thanks all —
Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Head of Account Strategy | Redwood Inference
Attachments: mutual_action_plan_v2.docx; acme_sla_clause_redline.pdf
